content.title: Boundary-Crossing Route | Preserve the Carrier Through a Material World Shift
content.summary: Establish one stable moving carrier, its route direction, and its camera relationship before a single boundary event rewrites the surrounding material world. Preserve orientation and motion continuity through the shift, pass readable landmarks in the new environment, and end with an explicit arrival action and held destination state. This is new evidence for the existing route-continuity selector, not a duplicate selector.

quick_start.input_format: continuous moving carrier + original-world baseline + one global material shift + preserved direction and speed + destination in the new world
quick_start.recommended_input: An original triangular ceramic survey glider with one amber core moves steadily rightward over a charcoal map membrane. The same glider crosses curling black vapor and floating graphite fragments while its amber core remains visible, then opens two ceramic braking wings, aligns once, locks into a hexagonal receiving socket, and holds to prove arrival.
required_anchors: Establish one stable carrier, route direction and camera relationship before the boundary changes.
Use one visible boundary event that causally opens the new material environment.
Reveal and preserve one destination after the new world becomes readable.
End with one explicit arrival action and a held terminal state.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Establish one stable moving carrier, its route direction, and its camera relationship before a single boundary event rewrites the surrounding material world. Preserve orientation and motion continuity through the shift, pass readable landmarks in the new environment, and end with an explicit arrival action and held destination state. This is new evidence for the existing route-continuity selector, not a duplicate selector.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Lock one original carrier, one route direction and one forward-tracking relationship before any transformation. Use one causally triggered boundary breach to convert the surrounding material world while the carrier's identity, heading and motion remain continuous. Preserve a readable destination through the new geography and end on an explicit arrival action followed by a stable hold. The reusable mechanism is route continuity through world conversion and terminal arrival, not the source seabird, tiled wall, ocean vortex, lighthouse, sunset, exact flight path, watermark or prompt wording.

invariants.rule: Establish one stable carrier, route direction and camera relationship before the boundary changes.
invariants.purpose: Creates a continuity baseline that survives the world conversion.
invariants.ablation_failure: Beginning inside the transformed world makes the transition unprovable.

invariants.rule: Use one visible boundary event that causally opens the new material environment.
invariants.purpose: Connects the two worlds through an attributable action.
invariants.ablation_failure: An unrelated cut becomes ordinary montage.

invariants.rule: Keep carrier identity, heading and forward progress continuous through the turbulent middle state.
invariants.purpose: Prevents the transformation from replacing the subject or route.
invariants.ablation_failure: Direction reversal or identity drift breaks the travel logic.

invariants.rule: Reveal and preserve one destination after the new world becomes readable.
invariants.purpose: Gives the converted route a concrete objective.
invariants.ablation_failure: Changing landmarks every shot creates spectacle without navigation.

invariants.rule: End with one explicit arrival action and a held terminal state.
invariants.purpose: Proves the route completed rather than merely continuing.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending mid-flight leaves the mechanism open.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source white seabird, feathers, anatomy, flight poses and exact identity
the source off-white tiled wall, crack pattern, flying white shards and paper-like fragments
the source blue ocean vortex, lighthouse, rocks, sunset, lantern gallery and exact destination composition
the source shot timing, route, camera orbit, landing choreography and warm-cool grade
the source churvikv and DreaminaAI watermark, model labels and creator prompt wording
